$comment: Deterministic per-server ranker regression cases (#205, Part 1). Every expectation here was OBSERVED against the shipped ranker, never guessed: each case was run through the real {platform}_search_tools tool over the MCP wire before being written down. See evals/tool-search-ranking.test.mjs for how they are driven, and the README section in that file for what this does and does not prove.
$layer: This covers Layer 1 only — packages/shared/src/utils/tool-search.ts, which searches ONE server's own registry and is a pure deterministic function of text we hand-edit. Layer 2 (a client's model choosing across the merged tools/list of several servers) is where genuine cross-server confusion lives, is not reachable from here, and needs a model-based harness on a schedule. Part 1 does not block on it.

cases.query: download the finished report as a CSV
cases.note: The issue's own flagship example. ttd_download_report scores 23; the next four tools tie at 14, so only the top slot is meaningfully pinned here.
Deleting the entity must outrank deleting a report schedule — the two are one token apart and msads gets this backwards (see gaps).

Deliberately pinned even though the generic update tool loses. A dedicated budget-schedule tool IS the better answer for a budget query, so this ordering is the one worth protecting — not an accident to be corrected.
Pins that video beats image for a video query — the two differ by one name token and share most of their description.
TTD is the one server whose archive path has 'archive' in the tool name, so the lexical ranker finds it. Contrast dv360, whose archive path is bulk_update_status — see gaps.

Promoted from gaps. 'remove' shares no word with 'delete', so the delete tool used to score 1 and dv360_get_pacing_status won. The ranker now reads 'remove' as 'delete' (QUERY_SYNONYMS in tool-search.ts): dv360_delete_entity scores 11 and the pacing tool falls to 4.

Promoted from gaps (the same synonym fix, on a second server). Pinned as top-2 rather than top-1 on purpose: ttd_delete_entity and ttd_delete_report_schedule tie at 10, and the tie goes to registry order, so asserting #1 would pin tools/list order instead of the ranker.

Promoted from gaps. The query word 'ad' used to substring-match 'adjust', which gave tiktok_adjust_bids the full +5 name weight. Names are now split into words and a prefix match needs at least 3 characters, so 'ad' matches the word 'ad' and nothing inside 'adjust'.

Promoted from gaps[] once msads_delete_report_schedule's description began with 'NOT SUPPORTED' (Microsoft Advertising Reporting has no schedules) and stopped picking up description hits. The margin is a TIE (9–9) resolved by registry order, so reordering allTools can flip it — the thinnest pinned case in the corpus.

gaps.note: The safety case #205 asks about. Narrowed but still open: 'remove' now reaches delete, so dv360_delete_entity went from outside the top 6 to #2 (12). dv360_adjust_line_item_bids still wins at 22, because 'line' and 'item' each match a word in its name for +5. Both of dv360's irreversible paths (delete, and archive via bulk_update_status) are terminal per #201. Beating an object noun that appears in a tool's name needs the query's operation to outweigh it, and rarity (IDF) weighting was tried and rejected: it broke 3 protected cases by amplifying repeated description words.
A read-only forecasting tool outranks the delete tool for an explicit delete query, on the strength of 'campaign' appearing in its name. amazon_dsp_delete_entity is #2.
